item.description: Duke Energy has offered Highlands County Emergency Management $15,000 to support the Emergency Operations Center. Emergency Management would use the money to buy watercraft for flood response. Flooding in Highlands County can leave residents stranded in neighborhoods that ground vehicles cannot reach. This shows up during tropical systems and heavy rain events, including the flooding this month. Watercraft would let responders reach stranded residents, rescue them, and help with evacuations when roads are underwater or impassable. Having this equipment on hand would make the county's flood response faster and safer for both residents and responders.

item.description: Highlands County currently operates seven WeatherSTEM stations across the county. The County asked for additional stations through this agreement with the Florida Division of Emergency Management (FDEM), and FDEM approved one. The new station will be installed at the Highlands County Landfill. WeatherSTEM stations send real-time weather data to Highlands County Emergency Management, the National Weather Service, and FDEM. item.description: Florida Statutes, Chapter 406, requires that the County arrange for the final disposition of human remains at the expense of the public when the remains are unclaimed or when a decedent qualifies as indigent. Highlands County recognizes its responsibility to provide for the dignified disposition of eligible indigent and unclaimed human remains when no other person or entity has both the legal responsibility and financial ability to do so. Highlands County has established a "Cremation Only" practice which means that disposition of human remains at the expense of the County shall be only through the use of cremation, except when prohibited by law or regulations and/or the identity of the decedent is unknown.
